matches.evidence: 26 GPP NetCDF means cover 1859-1899 and 2259-2299 for 13 ESMs and explicitly identify GPP in kg m-2 y-1. Nine accompanying point shapefiles identify candidate dieback cells. Annual grids and tabular GPP support the calculation. First four records in each of 12 models verified that mean19th/mean23rd in filtered2-npp.xlsx equal corresponding GPP mean-grid values; matching numeric values occur in the _change.xlsx family.
matches.limitations: The nine shapefiles contain points with FID only, not polygon areas or a loss field. Sampling all 292 points against their paired GPP means found 292 future/past ratios below 0.30 but only 234 below 0.20; therefore they do not all satisfy the spreadsheet definition of over 80% decrease. The 24 summary tables have misleading npp filenames, require a coordinate/ID join, and _change IDs were one lower in the inspected pairs. Grids are global, not already clipped to the Amazon. Other periods, climate/NPP means, Koppen classes and regional summaries are separate outputs without matching dataset descriptions. Variable time bounds, inherited historical metadata, calendars and model-specific licensing still need validation before catalog publication.

matches.evidence: All 28 suitability CSVs were individually assigned: current species/group tables and future complete/migratory/sedentary tables for 245/585 and 2030/2050/2070/2090. Species-coded continuous suitability values and coordinate-enriched files match the substance of the row.
matches.limitations: Delivered format is tabular grids, not a supplied raster distribution map. Binary presence/absence and thresholds are not identified. Current CSVs use mixed delimiters and not all include explicit latitude/longitude. Paper baseline dates and scenario-year semantics require preservation separately from filenames.

matches.evidence: Six WBGTid_COR-mdmx_AS_MesMax scenario NetCDF files provide warmest-month in-shade WBGT climatology for historical/RCP4/RCP8 with forested and deforested conditions. Each contains wbgt with shape 1 x 1 x 278 x 222 over South America. The municipal WBGT table is an interpolated derivative; ERA5 is a comparison/input grid.
matches.limitations: All six files store the same nominal 1987 time, including future scenarios, and the wbgt variable lacks units. Coverage years and degrees Celsius come from the sheet and naming, not a validated CF time axis. Scenario differences and regional daily/nighttime distributions are additional outputs, separately listed as unmatched to the supplied dataset descriptions.

matches.evidence: Sixteen scenario CSVs directly contain Average_Energy_MW, Firm_Energy_MW and TotalSpills. Every file has 42 rows: six historical model/downscaling combinations and 36 future combinations. The matching KNN subset has three GCMs, two SSPs and three future climatologies. Discharge scenario files are identified as hydropower inputs by the workbook-generation code.
matches.limitations: The package also includes BCSD results outside the sheet KNN count. Land-management files use E0/E1/E2/E4 codes; final mapping to paper scenario names needs a lookup. Climatology codes 0-3 do not by themselves establish complete source periods: crop/discharge summaries start in 2000, and code boundaries use 2015/2045/2075. No full daily power time series was identified, but the described mean/firm-power outcomes are delivered.

matches.evidence: Forty-one source NetCDFs are supplied: 38 GCM precipitation/temperature inputs plus three PISCO datasets, with selection/downscaling scripts and PISCO reports. Results/Climate data contains no non-OS files. No standalone set of 18 KNN future climatologies and four backcasts was located.
matches.limitations: Original GCM/PISCO inputs are not the downscaled product described. GCM names in the input package differ from the MIROC6/MPI result families. Prior metadata inspection flagged the PISCO precipitation time axis and a 20-year GFDL historical-temperature gap; assess these before reuse. Reproducing the outputs was outside this read-only matching review.

matches.evidence: Forty-eight CropYield CSVs plus 16 workbooks and 48 TotalCropYield CSVs plus 16 workbooks provide annual scenario crop yield and complementary total-production aggregates. All CSVs were checked for coverage: 2000-2014 historical and 2019-2099 future. Sample workbooks contain historical/ssp126/ssp585 sheets with the same model/downscaling columns. Landuse_analysis_library.R extracts SWAT HRU YLD, aggregates potato classes over selected Chaglla subbasins and exports annual results.
matches.limitations: The sheet period 1985-2014 is only partly delivered and future summaries stop in 2099, not 2100. The code includes POTA plus half-weighted POSE production; confirm agronomic meaning and reporting units. Both KNN and BCSD are present. XLSX/CSV formats overlap and should not be counted as independent datasets. These files do not deliver HRU-specific daily values.
matches.title_as_supplied: Sustainable land and irrigation management to limit loss of hydropower in the Andes-Amazon headwaters
matches.paper_verification_notes: Publisher indexed article metadata gives publication and version of record on 18 November 2024, Communications Earth & Environment 5, article 648. Direct opening encountered a cookie redirect.

matches.description: Modelled crop yields of potatoes, the dominant crop in the region and what we used to represent food sector performance, calculated by SWAT on a daily time-step over 1371 hydrologic response units of the upper Huallaga Basin under 16 landuse/management scenarios and 18 climate scenarios.

All CSVs were checked for coverage: 2000-2014 historical and 2019-2099 future. Sample workbooks contain historical/ssp126/ssp585 sheets with the same model/downscaling columns. Landuse_analysis_library.R extracts SWAT HRU YLD, aggregates potato classes over selected Chaglla subbasins and exports annual results.
